comment: What must not silently disappear from skillhelp. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces; `split` declares which half of the skill is deterministic; `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run.

prose.pattern: Never answer ungrounded: every fact this skill emits carries
prose.rationale: The one rule. It is the reason this skill exists rather than a prompt; lose the line and the skill becomes a generic assistant with extra steps.

prose.pattern: Never claim a result you did not observe
prose.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

prose.pattern: never ask about anything in it
prose.rationale: Two questions maximum is only achievable because detection already answered the rest. Asking about a detectable signal is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form.

deterministic.step: extract the five sections and their file:line sources from every skill's own files, refusing secret-shaped lines
prove no card would change, no skill is uncovered, and no fact has lost its source
route a question to grounded facts, or emit the not-documented block naming what was searched
list every skill with its version and trigger phrases

nondeterministic.step: disambiguating which skill the user means when the question names none, or names several
nondeterministic.why: a question like "how do I cut a release" spans release, shipflow and skillfactory, and only intent decides which one is being asked about

nondeterministic.step: writing the answer prose from the retrieved facts, in the right order and at the right length
nondeterministic.why: a card is a set of grounded facts, not an answer; which three of eleven facts matter, and whether the user wants a command or an explanation, is judgment

nondeterministic.step: judging whether a retrieval that scored above the floor actually answers the question asked
nondeterministic.why: the retrieval command can prove a fact exists and came from a real line, but not that it is responsive; a near-miss relayed as an answer is the ungrounded failure wearing a citation

_baseline_comment: Pinned against a real run of this skill, never a synthetic fixture. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, so CI cannot spend and cannot flake.

baseline.rationale: an extractor silently dropping a section so a card still looks complete while answering nothing; a fact losing its file:line source, which is what makes every answer built on it ungrounded — pinned against a frozen snapshot of real source files from this repo's shipped skills, copied in at freeze time and rebuilt on every test run, byte-compared card for card — a real run over real files whose input is pinned, so the golden moves only when the extractor moves and not when any of sixteen skills is edited.

routing degrading until every question returns the same handful of skills, or returns nothing while still exiting zero — a retriever that matches nothing looks identical to a question with no answer; and the not-documented block decaying into an empty result the caller renders as confidence — pinned against a frozen set of real questions actually asked of this repo's skills, resolved against the same pinned snapshot and byte-compared, including two questions whose correct result is the not-documented block.

the drift gate weakening until a stale card answers with full confidence, and equally the gate becoming so noisy it reddens on edits that change no answer — the two-sided half of build-golden, which alone would go green the day check stopped checking — pinned against a snapshot skill mutated in a way that changes its card, a snapshot skill mutated only in a comment that changes no card, and a skill present with no card at all.

the skill resolver matching nothing and reporting a fully-covered, fully-fresh index over zero skills — pinned against every skill shipped in this repo as a live corpus, with an anti-vacuity floor of 12 while exact coverage is check's job, so a removed skill is not a false failure.

the grounding requirement decaying into decoration — a sourceless fact reaching a card instead of being dropped — and the extractor lifting a credential out of a skill's scripts into a committed, published index — pinned against a card fact stripped of its source, and a snapshot skill whose files contain a secret-shaped line.
